problem: Evaluation of MLLM-based (vision-driven) embodied agents is underexplored. Prior LLM-agent benchmarks are mostly text-only (AgentBench, Lota-Bench, Embodied Agent Interface). VisualAgentBench covers only high-level planning, so it cannot answer what role vision plays or how MLLMs handle low-level navigation and manipulation. Prior benchmarks also report only overall accuracy, not capability-level diagnostics.
motivation: Off-the-shelf MLLMs are increasingly used as embodied planners, and comparing them requires a standardized, automated suite. That suite should span both high-level skill planning and low-level atomic control, and should separate distinct abilities: commonsense, complex-instruction understanding, spatial awareness, visual perception and long-horizon planning. The authors suspect that high-level benchmarks under-measure vision, because text alone may suffice there.
key_idea: Build a 1,128-task, four-environment benchmark with hierarchical action levels (EB-ALFRED and EB-Habitat for high-level skills, EB-Navigation and EB-Manipulation for low-level atomic actions) and six capability-oriented subsets, and evaluate 24 frozen MLLMs through one unified multi-step-planning agent pipeline.
insight: 1) Vision matters for low-level control but barely for high-level planning. Removing images (the 'Lang' rows) drops GPT-4o on EB-Navigation from 57.7 to 17.4, with the Long subset falling to 0.0. On EB-ALFRED, GPT-4o (Lang) actually scores higher (58.0 vs 56.3). Language-side ablations on the EB-ALFRED base subset confirm text dominates: removing environment feedback costs about 10% for GPT-4o, and 0-shot in-context learning drops success to about 40%. 2) Long-horizon planning is the hardest subset everywhere; e.g., Claude-3.5-Sonnet falls from 96 (Base) to 58 (Long) on EB-Habitat. 3) Visual-centric ablations on the EB-Manipulation base subset: 500×500 images beat both 300×300 and 700×700; removing detection boxes drops GPT-4o from 39.6 to 27.1; multi-step image history confuses current MLLMs; two visual in-context examples beat text-only ICL (Claude-3.5-Sonnet +16.7%). For EB-Navigation, keeping chat/interaction history helps most models (GPT-4o 57.7 vs 45.3 without it, Long subset 55.0 vs 15.0).
method: Four environments: (a) EB-ALFRED is built on ALFRED/AI2-THOR from Lota-Bench's simulator, fixed to support multiple same-type instances, with merged put-down actions and manually corrected instructions; its dynamic action space has 171–298 high-level skills (find/pick up/open/close/turn on/off/slice/put down). (b) EB-Habitat is built on Language Rearrangement/Habitat 2.0 with 70 parameterized skills, and navigation is restricted to receptacles. (c) EB-Navigation is built on AI2-THOR with 8 low-level actions: move forward/back/left/right by Δx, rotate by Δθ, tilt camera by Δφ; there is no position information, success means reaching within a distance of the target, and tasks are auto-generated by script. (d) EB-Manipulation extends VLMBench with a 7-D arm action discretized into 100 position bins and 120 orientation bins.

Capability-oriented subsets: Base, Common Sense, Complex Instruction, Spatial Awareness, Visual Appearance and Long Horizon. EB-ALFRED and EB-Habitat each have 300 tasks (50 per subset). EB-Navigation has 300 tasks (60 per subset, no Spatial subset). EB-Manipulation has 228 tasks (48 per subset, 36 for Visual, no Long subset). Data sources: manual annotation plus GPT-4o augmentation (EB-ALFRED, EB-Manipulation), a reorganized existing dataset (EB-Habitat), and fully programmatic generation (EB-Navigation).

Unified vision-driven agent input: language instruction, the current egocentric image (500×500), text in-context examples (10 by default for high-level tasks), interaction history, environment textual feedback (action validity, collisions, failure reasons) and task-specific information (valid skill set or action-format description). EB-Navigation additionally keeps chat history.

Structured multi-step task planner: at each planning call the MLLM outputs JSON containing (1) a visual description, (2) a reflection on past actions and feedback, (3) reasoning, (4) a language plan, and (5) an executable multi-action plan of variable length. Replanning from the latest state happens on failure or invalid action, which cuts API calls compared with one action per step.
Manipulation grounding aids: YOLO detection boxes with Set-of-Mark index markers plus pose estimates for indexed objects are given, so the MLLM does not need to infer precise 3D locations.

Evaluation protocol: 24 MLLMs (8 proprietary, 16 open-source, 7B–90B) at temperature 0 with max 2048 output tokens. Step limits are 30 for high-level tasks, 20 for EB-Navigation and 15 for EB-Manipulation. Metrics are task success rate plus subgoal success rate for the high-level tasks. A 'Lang' condition removes the image to test the role of vision, and a manual error taxonomy covers perception, reasoning and planning errors.

setting.backbone: 24 frozen MLLMs, e.g. GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-08-06), Claude-3.5/3.7-Sonnet, Gemini-1.5-Pro/2.0-flash, Qwen-VL-Max, InternVL2.5/3 (8–78B), Qwen2/2.5-VL (7B/72B), Llama-3.2-Vision (11B/90B), Ovis2, Gemma-3
setting.training_data: none (training-free); prompting with text in-context examples (10 by default for high-level tasks; 2 visual ICL examples in ablation)
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB (500×500) + textual environment feedback + interaction history; EB-Manipulation adds YOLO boxes with index markers and object pose estimates
setting.action_space: High-level skill APIs in EB-ALFRED (171–298 actions) and EB-Habitat (70 skills). EB-Navigation: 8 low-level actions (move forward/backward/left/right Δx, rotate left/right Δθ, tilt up/down Δφ). EB-Manipulation: discretized 7-D end-effector action (100 position bins, 120 rotation bins, gripper). Multi-action plans are emitted per planning call.
setting.privileged: EB-Navigation: none (no position data). High-level tasks use skill APIs such as 'find X' or 'navigate to receptacle' that abstract away navigation. EB-Manipulation provides detection boxes and object pose estimates for indexed objects.

numbers_note: All four benchmarks are new and the paper's own; there is no official split, so 'test' is used. Rows are MLLMs plugged into the paper's agent pipeline, so only representative models are listed; Tables 2 and 3 contain all 24 models. Some ablations appear only in figures without printed values: resolution, multi-step images, visual ICL and in-context example count (the EB-ALFRED 0-shot result is given only as 'around 40%'). An appendix table on EB-Navigation detection-box strategies (GPT-4o: No Box 61.7, One Box 68.3, Multi Box 53.3) does not state which subset it uses. The subgoal success-rate table omits Claude-3.7, InternVL3, Qwen2.5-VL, Ovis2 and Gemma-3. The text states Claude-3.5-Sonnet has the highest high-level accuracy, yet Table 2 shows Claude-3.7-Sonnet higher on EB-ALFRED (67.7 vs 64.0).
results: MLLMs perform well on high-level tasks but poorly on low-level ones. On high-level tasks the best average is Claude-3.7-Sonnet at 67.7 on EB-ALFRED and Claude-3.5-Sonnet at 68.0 on EB-Habitat. GPT-4o leads the low-level tasks with 57.7 on EB-Navigation but only 28.9 on EB-Manipulation. The best open-source model, InternVL3-78B, nearly matches GPT-4o on low-level tasks (53.7 on EB-Navigation, 26.3 on EB-Manipulation), yet trails on high-level ones (39.0 on EB-ALFRED). Removing vision collapses low-level performance (GPT-4o on EB-Navigation drops 57.7→17.4), while high-level performance is unchanged or slightly better. Long-horizon subsets are consistently the hardest. In error analysis, planning errors dominate (55% on EB-ALFRED, 44% on EB-Manipulation), and perception errors are much more common on EB-Manipulation (33% vs 4%).
limitations: Simulation only, with no real-robot evaluation.

The high-level tasks rely on text-rich skill APIs and in-context examples, so they barely test vision (the language-only agent matches or beats the vision agent). EB-Navigation is a short-range, single-room AI2-THOR object-goal task with a 20-step budget, not large-scale or continuous VLN.

EB-Manipulation depends on YOLO boxes and object pose estimates, and some subsets are missing (no Spatial subset in EB-Navigation, no Long subset in EB-Manipulation). Only a single fixed agent pipeline is evaluated, with small subsets (48–60 tasks each).
